reviews.review:
This game is awesome!

Overview (TL;DR): A great game, especially on sale. Gives you the feeling of being a space marine perfectly. The combat feels awesome, and is incredibly brutal. Besides some minor game play things (and the touch of matt ward) the game is by far worth the purchase. The only major downside is that the multiplayer is dead, but it's not the best anyway. Easily in my top ten games.

Positives:
The games art design is amazing, The backgrounds have a tendency to fall in the trap of the gray-brown cholor scheme typical of the time which is a drawback but it's actually very appropiate. The enemy designs are actually very colorful, along with your own troops, so it balances out and imo is how it's optimal as the orcs are very easy to spot and engage. Also they nail that blend of gothic, latin and sci-fi art design perfectly so it should appeal to veteren fans.

The combat in this game is great. It's very much a hack and slash all the way to the end, but it never stops being visceral and engaging with new enemy types being fed at a decent pace. They also feel different, and are usually easy to distinguish (the rokkit boyz look almost excatly like their basic ♥♥♥♥♥ counterparts idk why). The missions are not always the same and the variation is typically welcome and well placed. They also don't take very long so if you're not into a particular mix-up then you'll move on relatively quickly. If you are into that mix-up then don't worry either, because they recycle some of them. There are also very visually appealing boss fights and they tend to differ from each enough to be enjoyable (although none particularly memorable as they aren't very inspired boss ideas). 

Although captain titty is a mary sue, he still manages to feel like an actual marine. That's my favorite part of the game, for I AM THE EMPORERS INSTRUMENT, THE ENFORCER OF HIS WILL, ANGEL OF DEATH, I WILL PURGE THE HERETIC...

If you can find a match, definitely check out the multiplayer. It's not the best but it is fun to pick up every now and then. I bought this on 360 back at launch, and I probably got another 30-40 hours over the years I had that console out of the multiplayer.

All the melee weapons feel pretty different and fun. (The ranged ones not so much but it's forgivable.)

Negatives:
If you're looking for a gripping 40k story then look elsewhere. This is beyond stock standard for 40k tropes, so much so that before I knew anything about 40k lore I had already predicted the games ending. None of the characters are that great or memorable but the orcs voice acting will keep you going. (my favorite is when they scream AROOGA as you dismember them FOR THE EMPORER). Also, you play as the ultramarines and IDK if matt ward had his hands on this script but it feels like it. Captain Titty and his merry band of stereotypes are all ultramarines and they fit the bill, sadly. (mary sues whooooo).

The game has horrible pacing outside of enemy types. I know I also said the mix up's aren't bad but one of them in particular felt like the whole game got derailed. (a weird psuedo-stealth cover based mission against turrents that feels way too long.) You'll go from one mission where there's virtually no dialogue and just nonstop blood shed into a mission where all just talk, and talk, and talk. Normally I'm not against heavy-handed story telling but if your games story is ♥♥♥♥♥ it probably doesn't deserve to slow down the amazing game play. Also, the bosses are kind of weak and weird until the end. They are fun, but usually they kind of halt the flow of the game and generally aren't that cool until the fourth act.

The game is dead online for the most part.

This game isn't hard at all. I remember struggling with it as a kid, which makes me feel pretty embarresed because I picked this up now on hard mode with absolutely no difficulty. Typically when I play a game on hard, I want it to force me to really take in the game. Learn its mechanics, enemy types, etc. Thats really not the case with this, you're pretty much an ultrawoodchipper regardless. The only time I ever felt the game was 'hard' was in areas of little to no cover and lots of aoe enemies. The rockets generally get you in two - three hits, so if anything it's more cheese difficulty then actually making the game feel 'harder'.

These controls are not natural.
I didn't give this game a chance until years after i purchased it because it just didn't feel right.
That was a mistake, this game 'feels' right. You stomp around like a badass, bolter rounds quite literally have weight to them. No game has done the spess mehrines justice like this one. 
If you have a few friends the co-op mode is a blast, the story (so far, as i am currently progressing) is quite good also, the main downside with an older game like this is no online activity....at all. Regardless this is just a good time, turn your brain off and blast some orcs.

I have never played a Warhammer 40k game before, and after playing Space Marine, I feel like I have been missing out. Space Marine is so much fun, you feel like a holy death machine.  The campaign allbeit short, is enjoyable with a good story line.  Its never too challenging and its always a blast to replay.  Carving through hordes of Orks with devastating melee and ranged weapons never felt so satisfying.  The combat is smooth and precise, and the finishing moves are brutal.  The graphics are good still to this date, and the attention the detail is suprising.  Online is still active, you can find full games daily in Versus and Coop.  Both modes are very fun and challenging.  The customizeable classes and armors personalizes the gameplay, and urges you to rush your Space Marine into battle.  I really enjoyed my time playing this game and I dont see any reason why you wouldnt either.  For the Emperor!

This game rocks. Don't know much about the Warhammer 40,000 universe but I still had a blast. Great campaign, fun weapons, Titus is badass and the soundtrack is tight. Hope people continue to play the game and its multiplayer cause its tons of fun.
